messages:
maria: quick heads-up — after the RBAC rollout at 22:30 UTC we started seeing DSAR delete jobs hit a retention-exception path for EU accounts. Not a full outage but requests are being queued for legal review. @sec-oncall please advise :eyes:

jake: confirmed. delete-worker logs show KMS decrypt failures (403-ish) when trying to unseal tombstone keys, then we fallback to retention-exception. snippet:
```
2026-03-20T22:31:12Z delete-worker ERROR key_unseal: access denied for key "projects/redwood/keystore/eu/embeddings"
http status: 403
request_id: delete-9a2f
```

oliver: who rolled RBAC changes? was it the service-account scope change from last deploy?

maria: deployments show the change was the new least-priv SA policy (embed-deleter@redwood). It removed kms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt outside-prod. rollout notes: `sa:embed-deleter -> removed k[decrypt]`

alisha: if decrypt permission removed, KMS throws and we can't produce proof-of-deletion -> legal path. We should be able to short-circuit for DSARs by granting a scoped ephemeral grant via keystore-proxy.

sec-oncall: for triage — two parallel actions: 1) re-add decrypt to embed-deleter for EU until we rotate to ephemeral grants (rollback ACL), 2) add an audit flag for DSAR-delete flows so we can prove operation and avoid retention-exception if proof exists. Any objections? :+1:

legal: we need a written trail before we re-grant perms. Can we do a temporary exception with evidence snapshots (S3: s3://privacy-proofs/eu-delete/1789991234/) and an approval ticket in Zendesk? If so, proceed.

deploy-bot: rollout 2026-03-20T22:25 UTC -> rbacs/service-accounts patch applied by jake. Patch id: rb-2026-03-20-77

jake: I'll open a rolling rollback PR to re-add `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` for embed-deleter scoped to the EU keystore. Also adding immediate audit log marker: `event:dsar_delete_attempt -> proof_bucket`.

oliver: for longer term, let's create a patch to keystore-proxy to request a short-lived decrypt grant (5m) scoped to DSARs. That avoids giving broad decrypt rights to a service account. Also add a boolean `dsar_flow=true` in audit logs.

alisha: I'll draft runbook steps: 1) rollback perm 2) snapshot evidence to s3 3) legal sign-off 4) deploy proxy patch with tests 5) revoke broad perms. Expect ETA: 2 hours for rollback + evidence, 48h for proxy patch.

maria: thanks. tagging incident and privacy leads. I'll update the DSAR tracker and add links to PR + ticket. Filing follow-up: #privacy-playbook update to include ephemeral-grant pattern.

sec-oncall: assigning to jake for rollback and oliver for proxy PR. Please update thread when done.

jake: rolling back now. will post completion.

(approx 20m later)

jake: rollback done, perms re-added to embed-deleter for EU keystore. Evidence bucket created and populated. logs -> s3://privacy-proofs/eu-delete/1789991234/manifest.json

legal: received evidence, approving temporary exception. Keep us posted on proxy patch.

oliver: starting work on proxy grant. creating draft PR.

maria: great. closing triage loop for now. we'll treat this as a vuln-triage + policy gap: owner=platform-security, severity=low-medium, follow-up=proxy ephemeral grants + audit flag.
